_comment: Named experiments for run_scenario.py. Everything is data: add your own
scenario by copying a block, no Python changes needed.
rules       : rules PUT into the running app before the phases run
reset       : [[userId, component], ...] state keys cleared before the run
expect      : free text printed at the end, what you should observe
phases      : the traffic to generate, executed in order
sleep    : seconds to wait BEFORE the phase (optional)
user     : X-User-Id          (or users: [..] to spread across users)
delay    : seconds between requests (sequential mode only)

sequential-limit.description: Sequential requests exceeding a fixed window limit.

phases.name: 8 sequential requests against a limit of 5

sequential-limit.expect: The first 5 are allowed, the remaining 3 return HTTP 429.

window-expiry.description: Requests resume once the fixed window expires.

phases.name: Exhaust the 3 request window
Wait for the window to roll over, then retry

window-expiry.expect: Phase 1: 3 allowed then 2 limited. Phase 2: all 3 allowed again.

multiple-users.description: Independent users each get their own quota.

phases.name: user-a exhausts its quota
user-b is unaffected
user-c is unaffected

multiple-users.expect: user-a: 3 allowed + 2 limited. user-b and user-c: 3 allowed each.

free-vs-premium.description: The same API, two plans, two algorithms and two limits.

phases.name: FREE user, limit 5, FIXED_WINDOW
PREMIUM user, limit 20, TOKEN_BUCKET

free-vs-premium.expect: FREE: 5 allowed, 5 limited. PREMIUM: all 10 allowed.

multi-component.description: Two components with different rules do not share state.

phases.name: CODE_RUN: fixed window of 5 per 60s
CODE_SUBMIT: sliding window of 3 per 30s, same user

multi-component.expect: CODE_RUN: 5 allowed, 2 limited. CODE_SUBMIT: 3 allowed, 2 limited.

concurrent-same-user.description: The atomicity check: a burst from one user must not exceed the limit.

phases.name: 100 simultaneous requests from one user, limit 10

concurrent-same-user.expect: Exactly 10 allowed and 90 limited. Any other split means the decision is not atomic.

concurrent-different-users.description: Concurrent traffic from many users; each keeps its own quota.

phases.name: 10 users x 5 concurrent requests, limit 2 each

concurrent-different-users.expect: 20 allowed in total (2 per user) and 30 limited.

token-refill.description: A drained token bucket refills continuously over the window.

phases.name: Drain the bucket (capacity 6, refills 1 token/s)
After 3s, about 3 tokens have accrued
After another 6s the bucket is full again

token-refill.expect: Phase 1: 6 allowed, 2 limited. Phase 2: about 3 allowed. Phase 3: 6 allowed, 2 limited.

sliding-vs-fixed.description: The fixed window boundary burst, and how a sliding window prevents it.

phases.name: t=0s  one request each, opening the fixed window
t=0s  same for the sliding window endpoint
t=9s  4 more each, filling both to the limit of 5
t=9s  sliding window filled to 5 as well
t=11s FIXED_WINDOW just crossed its boundary - 5 more
t=11s SLIDING_WINDOW, identical traffic

sliding-vs-fixed.expect: FIXED_WINDOW allows all 5 at t=11s because the counter reset as a block - 9 requests inside ~2 seconds under a '5 per 10s' limit. SLIDING_WINDOW allows only 1, because the four requests from t=9s are still inside its window. Totals: 10 allowed for fixed, 6 for sliding.
